title: Inverse limits of a tower of short exact sequences whose kernels have surjective transition maps
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. For an inverse system $(P_n)_{n\ge1}$ of $R$-modules ($R$-linear transition maps $P_{n+1}\to P_n$, hence composites $P_m\to P_n$ for $m\ge n$) let $\varprojlim_nP_n\subseteq\prod_nP_n$ be the $R$-module of compatible sequences, with the coordinate projections $\varprojlim_nP_n\to P_m$. (a) If all transition maps $K_{n+1}\to K_n$ of an inverse system $(K_n)_{n\ge1}$ of $R$-modules are surjective, then every projection $\varprojlim_nK_n\to K_m$ ($m\ge1$) is surjective. (b) Let $0\to K_n\xrightarrow{u_n}B_n\xrightarrow{v_n}C_n\to0$, $n\ge1$, be short exact sequences of $R$-modules such that $(u_n)$ and $(v_n)$ are morphisms of inverse systems $(K_n)\to(B_n)\to(C_n)$ (they commute with the transition maps). Then $0\to\varprojlim_nK_n\xrightarrow{\varprojlim u_n}\varprojlim_nB_n\xrightarrow{\varprojlim v_n}\varprojlim_nC_n$ is exact, and if moreover all transition maps $K_{n+1}\to K_n$ are surjective, then $\varprojlim v_n$ is surjective, so that $0\to\varprojlim K_n\to\varprojlim B_n\to\varprojlim C_n\to0$ is exact.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 03CA (lemma-Mittag-Leffler) for (b), the system (K_n) with surjective transition maps satisfying its hypothesis with c(i) = i; Homology, Lemma 02N1 (homology-lemma-Mittag-Leffler, homology.tex) (1) and (3) with Definition 02N0 (homology-definition-Mittag-Leffler); (a) is used without proof in Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 087W (coherent.tex line 6290: 'As the transition maps are surjective, we see that M -> M_1 is surjective')

proof.text: (a) Write $f_n:K_{n+1}\to K_n$ for the transition maps and $\varphi_{n',n}=f_n\circ\cdots\circ f_{n'-1}:K_{n'}\to K_n$ ($n'\ge n$, the identity for $n'=n$) for their composites [def-weil-inverse-system]; $\varphi_{n'',n}=\varphi_{n',n}\circ\varphi_{n'',n'}$ for $n''\ge n'\ge n$. Fix $m\ge1$ and $k\in K_m$. Define $x_n\in K_n$ for all $n\ge1$: for $n\le m$ put $x_n=\varphi_{m,n}(k)$ (so $x_m=k$); for $n>m$ choose recursively $x_n\in K_n$ with $f_{n-1}(x_n)=x_{n-1}$, possible since $f_{n-1}$ is surjective (a recursive sequence of choices, made once for all $n$ by dependent choice). Then $f_n(x_{n+1})=x_n$ for every $n$: for $n\ge m$ by the choice of $x_{n+1}$; for $n<m$ because $f_n(x_{n+1})=f_n(\varphi_{m,n+1}(k))=\varphi_{m,n}(k)=x_n$. Hence $(x_n)_n$ is a compatible sequence, an element of $\varprojlim_nK_n$, and its projection to $K_m$ is $x_m=k$. So $\varprojlim_nK_n\to K_m$ is surjective.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 0597 (lemma-ML-limit-nonempty, line 20748) with Example 0596 (example-ML-surjective-maps, line 20736): the limit of a tower of nonempty sets with surjective maps is nonempty, by the axiom of choice; applied to the fibres of the composites over k, this is (a). Used in this form in Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 087W (coherent.tex line 6290)

proof.text: (b), the maps. Write $f^K_n,f^B_n,f^C_n$ for the transition maps of $(K_n),(B_n),(C_n)$; by hypothesis $f^B_n\circ u_{n+1}=u_n\circ f^K_n$ and $f^C_n\circ v_{n+1}=v_n\circ f^B_n$ [def-weil-inverse-system]. For $(x_n)\in\varprojlim_nK_n$ the sequence $(u_n(x_n))_n$ is compatible: $f^B_n(u_{n+1}(x_{n+1}))=u_n(f^K_n(x_{n+1}))=u_n(x_n)$; so $\varprojlim u_n:(x_n)\mapsto(u_n(x_n))$ is a well-defined map $\varprojlim K_n\to\varprojlim B_n$, $R$-linear since each $u_n$ is and the module operations on $\varprojlim\subseteq\prod$ are componentwise; likewise $\varprojlim v_n:(y_n)\mapsto(v_n(y_n))$. Their composite is $(x_n)\mapsto(v_n(u_n(x_n)))=0$, as $v_n\circ u_n=0$ for each $n$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence].

source.place: Algebra, Section 03C9 (section-inverse-systems, lines 20819--20845: the limit as compatible sequences) and proof of Lemma 0598 (lemma-ML-exact-sequence, line 20784: 'Taking limits of directed inverse systems is left exact')

proof.text: (b), injectivity of $\varprojlim u_n$. Each $u_n$ is injective, since $0\to K_n\to B_n\to C_n\to0$ is exact at $K_n$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. If $(u_n(x_n))_n=0$ then $u_n(x_n)=0$, hence $x_n=0$, for every $n$; so $(x_n)=0$.

source.place: Homology, Lemma 02N1 (lemma-Mittag-Leffler, line 7673) (1), whose proof is left as an exercise (line 7697); the left exactness is quoted in the proof of Algebra, Lemma 0598 (algebra.tex line 20784)

proof.text: (b), exactness at $\varprojlim B_n$. By step 2 the image of $\varprojlim u_n$ lies in the kernel of $\varprojlim v_n$. Conversely let $(y_n)\in\varprojlim B_n$ with $v_n(y_n)=0$ for all $n$. By exactness at $B_n$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] there is $x_n\in K_n$ with $u_n(x_n)=y_n$, unique since $u_n$ is injective (step 3). The sequence $(x_n)$ is compatible: $u_n(f^K_n(x_{n+1}))=f^B_n(u_{n+1}(x_{n+1}))=f^B_n(y_{n+1})=y_n=u_n(x_n)$, and $u_n$ is injective, so $f^K_n(x_{n+1})=x_n$. Thus $(x_n)\in\varprojlim K_n$ and $\varprojlim u_n((x_n))=(y_n)$. With steps 2 and 3, $0\to\varprojlim K_n\to\varprojlim B_n\to\varprojlim C_n$ is exact.

source.place: Homology, Lemma 02N1 (1) (line 7673), proof 'Nice exercise' (line 7697): the exercise is written out here

proof.text: (b), surjectivity of $\varprojlim v_n$ when all $f^K_n$ are surjective. Let $(c_n)\in\varprojlim C_n$, so $f^C_n(c_{n+1})=c_n$. We construct $b_n\in B_n$, $n\ge1$, recursively, such that $v_n(b_n)=c_n$ and $f^B_n(b_{n+1})=b_n$ for all $n$. Base: $v_1$ is surjective (exactness at $C_1$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]); choose $b_1$ with $v_1(b_1)=c_1$. Recursive step: let $b_n\in B_n$ with $v_n(b_n)=c_n$ be constructed. Choose $b'\in B_{n+1}$ with $v_{n+1}(b')=c_{n+1}$ ($v_{n+1}$ surjective). Then $v_n(f^B_n(b')-b_n)=f^C_n(v_{n+1}(b'))-c_n=f^C_n(c_{n+1})-c_n=0$, so by exactness at $B_n$ there is $k\in K_n$ with $u_n(k)=f^B_n(b')-b_n$. Since $f^K_n$ is surjective, choose $k'\in K_{n+1}$ with $f^K_n(k')=k$, and put $b_{n+1}=b'-u_{n+1}(k')$. Then $v_{n+1}(b_{n+1})=c_{n+1}-v_{n+1}(u_{n+1}(k'))=c_{n+1}$ (as $v_{n+1}\circ u_{n+1}=0$), and $f^B_n(b_{n+1})=f^B_n(b')-u_n(f^K_n(k'))=f^B_n(b')-u_n(k)=b_n$. The recursion only adds the term $b_{n+1}$ and never changes $b_1,\dots,b_n$, so (by dependent choice) it defines a sequence $(b_n)_{n\ge1}$ with both properties for every $n$. Then $(b_n)\in\varprojlim B_n$ and $\varprojlim v_n((b_n))=(v_n(b_n))=(c_n)$. (In the terms of the source: the fibres $E_n=v_n^{-1}(c_n)$ form a tower of nonempty sets, and the step shows that $E_{n+1}\to E_n$ is surjective, which is the Mittag-Leffler property of $(E_n)$ proved there, with $c(i)=i$ because $\operatorname{Im}(K_j\to K_i)=K_i$ for all $j\ge i$.)

proof.text: (b), conclusion. Steps 3 and 4 give the exactness of $0\to\varprojlim K_n\to\varprojlim B_n\to\varprojlim C_n$, and with step 5, when the $f^K_n$ are surjective, $\varprojlim v_n$ is surjective, so $0\to\varprojlim K_n\to\varprojlim B_n\to\varprojlim C_n\to0$ is a short exact sequence of $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] (exactness at each of the three terms).

lean.statement: theorem tower_limit_exact_surjective_kernels (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (F : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{v} R) (G : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{w} R) (H : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{t} R) (α : ∀ n : ℕ, F.obj (Opposite.op n) →ₗ[R] G.obj (Opposite.op n)) (β : ∀ n : ℕ, G.obj (Opposite.op n) →ₗ[R] H.obj (Opposite.op n)) (hα : ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : F.obj (Opposite.op (n + 1))), G.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_add_right n 1)).op (α (n + 1) x) = α n (F.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_add_right n 1)).op x)) (hβ : ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : G.obj (Opposite.op (n + 1))), H.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_add_right n 1)).op (β (n + 1) x) = β n (G.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_add_right n 1)).op x)) (hshort : ∀ n : ℕ, Function.Injective (α n) ∧ Function.Exact (α n) (β n) ∧ Function.Surjective (β n)) : ∃ (U : ↑(limit F) →ₗ[R] ↑(limit G)) (V : ↑(limit G) →ₗ[R] ↑(limit H)), (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : ↑(limit F)), limit.π G (Opposite.op n) (U x) = α n (limit.π F (Opposite.op n) x)) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : ↑(limit G)), limit.π H (Opposite.op n) (V x) = β n (limit.π G (Opposite.op n) x)) ∧ Function.Injective U ∧ Function.Exact U V ∧ ((∀ n : ℕ, Function.Surjective (F.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_add_right n 1)).op)) → Function.Surjective V)
